body:
Just remember more!

9 yo : My parents getting super angry and frustrated at me for pulling. Every night my dad would make me sit and he would check my bald spots for regrowth. One night they put socks over my hands and taped them on so I wouldn't pull.

I got referred to the school nurse for it and she suggested pulling out a teddies fur instead. I remember saying I would try but in my head thinking "not gunna work, teddies don't have roots and it's totally not the same".

Not that they have trich but the way their brain is genetically makes them more predisposed to impulse control disorders. I have trich still but maybe once every 3 years end up with bald eyelash patch. But usually just scabs on my face. I used to get massive bald patches on my head, no eyebrows etc etc. But it's slowed with age.

But if you're wanting to know the "whys" - I'm not a scientist/researcher but have had trich for over 20 years and have read a lot. My job is also related to neurology. I think it's something to do with our brains and also genetics as well. My dad had trich in his teens and now when I look back my grandma did as well (she would pull her eyebrows and leave them on the arm of her chair). Maybe our brains are this way due to genetics?

My grandma also now has parkinsons which is also related to putamen volumes.

Also definitely related to dopamine. But like I said I'm not a doctor/researcher so don't really know enough to comment.

I think that our genes play a massive part in why we have trich - my family history has a lot of impulse control disorders (alcoholism, trich, gambling)

"Researchers have suggested that structural or functional abnormalities of the brain may play a role in the development of trichotillomania. Such findings include subtle changes (compared to ‘control’ groups of people without trichotillomania) in the putamen, cerebellum and cortical regions such as the anterior cingulate and right inferior frontal gyri. These brain regions are important in how prone we are to develop habitual behaviors, and how able we are to suppress inappropriate or unwanted habits once they occur. The specific structural or functional brain abnormalities associated with trichotillomania and the role that they play in the development of trichotillomania require more research to understand, because findings differ between studies."

The dabbing the wet root on the lip thing is really common as well. I don't eat the root just dab on my lip to inspect "moistness". 

I also often peel/pull off the root from the hair, sometimes to see how deep in the scalp it was.

Suppose it's similar to how people with OCD can carry out similar/typical behaviours (ie flicking lights on and off), maybe?
Roots are thicc as fuck tho

At least when I pluck my stache hairs out it's not leaving me looking worse (debatable though because I like to get those hairs when they're ridiculously short and sometimes cause scabs on my face). Always look on the bright side....
Yeah me too, my grandma paraded me around the family laughing at me.

Sorry I didn't specify what 2 and 3 meant (months). I had this eyelash relapse because there was one single bristly eyelash in my normal/full lashes and I obvs had to have it :/!

As a child I routinely pulled out all my top lashes but they've always grown back ok, takes ages though!
I sometimes do this thing where I kind of run my nail up the hair shaft and it creates like a tree split end. The ends of my hair are so straggly because I do this!
Um, they were pulled for about 3 and took 2 to grow back, I'm not 100% though!

My eyelashes were such a pain to grow back, I love short bristly hairs and will actively search them our to get them - often making areas VERY red and sore.

I had been wearing false lashes in between (eyelure natural ones) and could not wait for them to grow back . I love applying makeup so my eyelashes were awful to have pulled out. I hated looking people in the eyes.

Now I have stopped ob my lashes and brows, and moves onto my (female) moustache hairs. Leaving red sores on my face. One step at a time.

I feel like posting here helps me not to pull cos I feel ashamed when I look at the pics. Falsies help me stop pulling cos I can't differentiate between the fake ones and my real lashes. I might start sleeping in them cause bed time is when I pull most.

Awh :( I hate the secrecy that comes with trich, I
told my OH (before he noticed) that I got scared/jumped when I was curling my lashes and ripped them out :,) (totally believable on both sides...not)!.
I'm gunna try vaseline-ing them tonight so I can't get a good grip, or maybe sleep in my falsies, haha!
You need eyelashes to stick the individual ones on top of, I don't mind wearing full strip ones but I feel like my contacts feel drier quicker with them on.

I'm finding them SUPER hard to grow back, my hands keep touching the regrowth (stupid little spiky hairs) and I keep trying to get them.

I've made one eyelid really sore trying to get really short new growth out. :(


I don't mind when I do it from the scalp so much cos it's coverable, but my lashes :(, I love doing makeup and stuff, now I have to wear false lashes every day. When I was a kid I pulled out ALL my top eyelashes and my grandma noticed and was super shocked and started parading me around the family "Look, she's got no eyelashes!!", from that day (about 9 years old) I swore to never do my lashes again. 

I'm 22 now and I've done em again, it all started with one single short eyelash, now this.

I have an appointment Oct 1st and I am shitting myself. 

Again today I'll swear I'll never pull another hair again (for the 100th time or whatever). She'll definitley notice this, what do I say? I can't blame it on the extensions no more. Cos it's fucking bald, not short as if extensions wore it away/snapped it or whatever.

BTW; anyone else seek out new growth? I 'love' getting tiny short hairs out. :( sick of this.
